chains.title: Ref C (G on the LMO1 sense strand) keeps an intact GATA motif bound by GATA3 in SK-N-SH, sustaining LMO1 expression in the adrenergic state

links.claim: The variant falls inside a GATA motif in LMO1 intron 1 (E06a/E09a); the reference C on the plus strand is G on the LMO1 sense strand, keeping the canonical GATA intact, while the alt A gives a TATA-type allele (E09b), so a GATA factor binds the reference allele more. Within the GATA binding-specificity group I pick GATA3 because an ENCODE GATA3 ChIP-seq peak in SK-N-SH (and in SH-SY5Y) contains this exact base (E07); no QBiC-SELEX row or qbic_tf_detail lookup for GATA3 was provided, so coverage is not_checked. The ref>alt direction is inferred from the motif conversion, not from measured allelic binding.

The base lies in a distal enhancer-like cCRE (EH38E1518342; DNase z 4.5, H3K27ac z 4.0, maxima across biosamples) at a highly conserved position (GERP 6.43); the GATA3 peak in SK-N-SH indicates the element is occupied in this cell line.
The enhancer acts on LMO1: the variant is intronic to LMO1 (nearest TSS 34.9 kb) and L2G gives LMO1 0.92 vs RIC3 0.08; the literature ties this SNP to LMO1 expression levels.

The effect is cell-state dependent: genome-edited zebrafish show the allele determines which core regulatory circuit is active, and the adrenergic state is the permissive one; SK-N-SH carries the GATA3 occupancy (E07).

GATA-allele-driven LMO1 expression promotes the adrenergic state and neuroblastoma initiation, so the TATA (alt A) allele is protective; the quote states that converting GATA to TATA reduced neuroblastoma initiation.

chains.title: Same GATA element, but GATA2 is the functionally dominant GATA factor in this context

links.claim: The motif changed is a GATA site (E06a/E09a/E09b) and all GATA factors share one binding specificity, so motif data cannot resolve the family member. GATA2 is chosen within the group on expression: it is at 133 TPM in SK-N-SH, rank 17 of 1626 TFs and the 97.3th percentile across DepMap lines (E08). The ENCODE peak at this base is a GATA3 experiment (E07), so direct occupancy evidence favours GATA3; GATA2 would have to co-occupy or compete. Coverage not_checked (no QBiC row or lookup).
The same distal enhancer-like cCRE with strong DNase/H3K27ac at a conserved base (GERP 6.43) is the element.
LMO1 is the regulated gene: intronic location and L2G 0.92 vs RIC3 0.08.
High GATA2 levels specifically in this neuroblastoma line make the element's output lineage-restricted; the allele-dependent circuit choice was shown in edited zebrafish.
Loss of GATA binding on the alt (TATA) allele lowers LMO1 and reduces neuroblastoma initiation, matching LMO1 variants being reported as protective.

chains.title: The alt A allele creates a TATA-type element that recruits a different factor and actively represses/retargets the enhancer, rather than merely losing GATA binding

links.claim: The cited mechanism describes conversion of the regulatory GATA allele to a 'TATA' allele (E09b); under this chain the alt A allele gains binding for a TATA-box-binding factor (TBP) rather than simply losing GATA. No motif scan, SELEX or ChIP row supports TBP occupancy here, so this binding claim is speculative; coverage not_checked.
The site is an active distal enhancer-like cCRE whose output could be redirected by a gained core-promoter-type element.
Whatever factor binds, the element's target remains LMO1 (intronic, L2G 0.92).
Allele-dependent circuit choice was shown in edited zebrafish, implying the effect is read out in neuroblastoma-competent cells.
If the alt allele gains a repressive/retargeting element, LMO1 stays low and neuroblastoma initiation is reduced, the same net protective direction.

predictions: A TATA-box/TBP footprint or peak appears only on the A allele

falsified_if: A-allele reporter activity equals a motif-scrambled control (pure loss of function)

grades_v0.reason: E06a says a G/T SNP affects a GATA motif in LMO1 intron 1, but it gives no TF identity or allele-specific binding data. E06b is a zebrafish allele-switch statement. GATA3 was picked on mechanism recall, with no ChIP, QBiC or expression row. Coverage 'not_checked' is shown by no lookup. Ref-binds-more direction is only inferred from the motif.
E03 places the variant inside dELS EH38E1518342 with DNase z 4.5 and H3K27ac z 4.0, and GERP is 6.43. These are maxima over biosamples, not SK-N-SH specific, so support is epigenomic context only.

E05 gives L2G of 0.92 for LMO1 vs 0.08 for RIC3, and E01/E02 show it is intronic to LMO1. These are genetic and positional, but no eQTL or CRISPR link is shown. The literature quote ties the SNP to LMO1 expression.

E06b is a zebrafish edit that determines which CRC is active, and E06a links the SNP to the adrenergic state through its title. Neither gives SK-N-SH-specific activity, because the cCRE z-scores are maxima over biosamples. 'Cell-state analyses' is not shown in any quote.

E06a links the SNP to both LMO1 expression and neuroblastoma risk, but the quote does not give the allele direction. E06c lists LMO1 as protective but names no variant. The claim that the ref allele raises risk is inferred. The GWAS Catalog rows (E04) are non-neuroblastoma traits.
The only evidence is E06a, which names no GATA2 binding. The claim rests on lineage expression recall, with no tf_expression or ChIP row. The coverage status is not shown by any lookup.
The same cCRE evidence as H1 (E03, E01) shows an active, conserved distal enhancer. It is not TF-specific.
E01 and E05 give an intronic position and L2G of 0.92 for LMO1. It is the same support as for H1.
E06b does not mention GATA2 or GATA3 activity in neuroblast-derived cells. The claim of cell-type restriction by GATA2 has no cited support.
E06a and E06c give general SNP-LMO1-risk context, but nothing ties GATA2 loss to lower LMO1 or lower risk. The allele direction is not stated.
E06b, a zebrafish statement, does not show an ETS site gain or FLI1 binding on the A allele. No motif, SELEX, ChIP or expression row is given. The coverage status is not shown by any lookup.
E03 supports an active enhancer, but not a switched circuit or an alt-allele-specific function.
L2G of 0.92 supports LMO1 as the local gene. It does not show that a repressive FLI1 effect acts on it.
E06b suggests that circuit choice depends on the allele in zebrafish, but it is not evidence for a mesenchymal-state cell type or for SK-N-SH.
Nothing cited shows that the alt allele engages a non-adrenergic circuit that keeps LMO1 low. E06c names no variant.

grades_final.reason: E06a/E09a/E09b show that this SNP changes a GATA motif, and E07 shows a GATA3 ChIP peak over the base in SK-N-SH. Neither is an allele-specific binding measurement, and GATA3 was chosen from a shared-specificity group on the basis of peak overlap only. The ref>alt direction is inferred from the motif conversion. The claim that C is G on the sense strand is not shown in the evidence. QBiC coverage was never looked up (suggest a qbic_tf_detail lookup for GATA3). E07 does not exclude GATA2 or GATA4 binding.

E03 places the variant inside dELS EH38E1518342 with strong DNase and H3K27ac signal (maxima over biosamples, not cell-specific), E01 gives GERP 6.43, and E07 shows GATA3 occupancy in SK-N-SH. This is epigenomic context only, but it directly shows an enhancer-like element at the base.

Open Targets L2G favours LMO1 (0.92 vs 0.08 for RIC3), the variant is intronic to LMO1 (E01/E02), and E06a ties the SNP to LMO1 expression. The literature link and the genetic prioritisation are consistent. No direct perturbation of this element is quoted, but the combination is solid.

E09c gives zebrafish genome-editing evidence that the allele determines which CRC is active, and E09b links the GATA allele to the adrenergic cell state. The claim that adrenergic is the permissive state is a partial inference from these. SK-N-SH GATA3 occupancy (E07) does not demonstrate state dependence. No evidence shows SK-N-SH is adrenergic or that the effect fails in other states.

E09b directly states that converting GATA to TATA at this LMO1 intron 1 allele reduced the neuroblastoma-initiation rate (perturbation). E06a and E06c are consistent with this. Direction is consistent: ref GATA drives risk and alt A is protective. The wording on LMO1 expression is slightly over-extended but the phenotype link is well supported.

The motif is GATA (E06a/E09b), but the only direct occupancy evidence at the base (E07) is GATA3, not GATA2, and the claim admits this. GATA2 was chosen from the shared-specificity group by expression rank (E08), which is context only. Coverage was not checked (suggest a qbic_tf_detail lookup for GATA2). Evidence for GATA2 binding at this element is lacking, so the link is at best weak.

E03 and E01 show a distal enhancer-like cCRE with strong DNase/H3K27ac at a conserved base containing the variant. The element is established independently of which TF binds. No GATA2-specific occupancy is shown, but that is not part of this claim.
Intronic location in LMO1 (E01) and L2G 0.92 vs 0.08 for RIC3 (E05) support LMO1 as the target, the same as in H1.

High GATA2 expression in SK-N-SH (E08) is expression context only and does not show that GATA2 acts at this element. E09c does not mention GATA2 and shows only zebrafish circuit choice. The claim that GATA2 expression makes the output lineage-restricted is over-claimed.

E09b says that GATA to TATA conversion reduced neuroblastoma initiation, and E06c reports LMO1 protective variants. Neither is attributed to GATA2, so the phenotype is tied to the allele rather than to this TF. The chain is consistent but indirect for GATA2. E06c does not name rs2168101 explicitly.

Nothing cited shows TBP or any other factor binding the alt A allele. The 'TATA' in E09b is a name for the allele, not evidence of TATA-box binding, and the claim concedes it is speculative. TBP is not supported by any screen row or lookup (suggest a qbic_tf_detail lookup for TBP). It also contradicts the cited loss-of-GATA mechanism.

E03 supports an active distal enhancer-like cCRE at the base. The claim that it could be redirected by a gained core-promoter element has no support in the evidence. Only the enhancer identity is established.
E01 (intronic to LMO1) and E05 (L2G 0.92) support LMO1 as the element's target, independent of which factor binds.
E09c supports only that edited zebrafish show allele-dependent circuit choice. It says nothing about a gained repressor or about neuroblastoma cells of either state, so this claim is generic.

E09b/E06c support reduced neuroblastoma initiation with the alt allele, so the direction is consistent. They do not support an active repression or retargeting mechanism, which is distinct from loss of GATA binding. The phenotype is borrowed from the H1 mechanism.
